pairs.question: Solum autem iugulat filios suos, an et torquet?
pairs.answer: Vtique per tormenta ignium et suppliciorum, per martyria fidei examinatoria.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical self-question: Tertullian asks whether divine Wisdom only slays her sons or also tortures them (real disjunctive interrogative with 'an'). The reply opens with a non-answering citation-framing preamble, 'Audio enim et alibi dicentem deum: uram illos sicut uritur aurum, et probabo illos sicuti probatur argentum' (scriptural grounds, narrated as a quotation), so the answer's start is advanced past that framing to the operative affirming sentence 'Vtique per tormenta...' ('Assuredly, by the torments of fires and punishments'), which directly answers 'yes, she also tortures.' Answer ends at the first full stop ('examinatoria.'); what follows ('Scit et apostolus...') turns to a new scriptural argument. Section marker [4] stripped from the answer span.
